anti_generic_signature_read: The two piece families are legible by silhouette alone, not colour - a clean regular hexagon with a three-way pyramid cap against a chaotic asymmetric rubble knot - and all four rubble pieces are one repeated sculpt. The tray outline is deliberately irregular, with unequal chamfered corners and slightly wobbling edges rather than a symmetric octagon, and the top face is broken into several near-flat facets instead of one plane. Generic by contrast: the plain cylinder disc feet and the uniform dished sockets.
blind_action_read: Two states of the same tray are shown side by side, with a single hex crystal on its disc hovering detached above and between them. Left panel: the top row has two hex pieces and one empty socket. Right panel: identical except that the top row's third socket is now occupied by a hex crystal. The floating piece is the one being added - the pair reads as a before and after of seating one crystal into the vacant top-right socket. Nothing else changes between panels.
blind_form_read: Overwhelmingly angular and faceted; everything is flat-shaded polygons. The base is a slab of flat planes with straight chamfered corner bevels, no fillets or round-overs anywhere. The pieces are hard-edged: hexagonal prisms with a six-facet pyramidal cap, and irregular blocky rubble with sharp wedge shards. Curvature is confined to the circular pocket rims and the cylindrical disc feet. No domes, spheres, lobes or spline surfaces; no fur, grit or micro-texture; the rubble carries a few knife-thin blade slivers. Nothing reads translucent - all opaque flat fill.
blind_held_read: A shallow, chunky tray or palette that fits in two hands: a thick slab of dark stone-brown material, roughly square with cut-off corners, with a raised lip and a sunken inner floor holding a 3x3 grid of round dished sockets. Each filled socket carries a small disc-footed piece: some are single faceted hexagonal gem-crystals, others are lumpy rubble clusters. It reads as a specimen tray or a board-game token board - heavy, low, meant to be set down and picked from.
blind_relationship_read: The tray is the host: its raised outer lip steps down to a recessed floor, and the nine circular dishes are sunk into that floor. Every small piece sits on its own round disc foot that drops into a dish, so the dish locates the piece; the pieces do not touch each other or the lip. The 3x3 array is regular and slightly rotated relative to the tray outline. Hex crystals and clusters are interleaved with no repeating stripe. In the signature sheet the floating crystal is above the plane, causally aimed at the one empty socket.
blind_subjects_read: Three kinds. One large base tray with nine round sockets. Five hexagonal capped crystals on round discs - top row left and right, middle row left, bottom row centre and right. Four rubble clusters on round discs - top centre, middle centre, middle right, bottom left. In the signature sheet the left panel shows the same tray with four pieces seated, two hex and two cluster, the right panel five, three hex and two cluster, plus one extra hex crystal floating free above the trays.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'every base surface is a flat plane meeting its neighbours at a hard crease: outer side walls, the corner cuts, the raised lip, the sloped inner wall and the recessed floor. Corners are straight chamfers, not fillets, and no blend or round-over appears at any edge. Apart from the circular pocket rims and the cylindrical disc feet of the small pieces, I can name no curve on the base.'
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The rind is a low-polygon fractured boulder: every outward and inward rock surface is a flat planar facet, facets meet at sharp visible edges, and no spline surface, fillet or round-over survives anywhere on the rock.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'the tray outline is deliberately irregular, with unequal chamfered corners and slightly wobbling edges rather than a symmetric octagon'. Primed measurement at the recovered 7.3750 px/mm scale: silhouette bounding box 140.20 x 130.17 mm, i.e. 140.00 x 130.00 within one pixel, over sixteen segments of 12.69 to 55.27 mm.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The plan outline is a closed polygon of twelve to sixteen straight segments of deliberately unequal length, angular and irregular rather than an even oval, measuring exactly 140.00 x 130.00 mm across its bounding box and centred on the origin.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Primed traverse: the rim-top outline is inset from the silhouette by 31-51 px sampled every 20 degrees, which over the 14 mm rise is 17-26 degrees from vertical and varies side to side. Sixteen wall planes plus the flat bottom and the flat rim top is eighteen outward facets, inside the fifteen-to-twenty aim; check_overhang at 45 degrees reports zero regions needing support.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The outer wall is flat planes at varying tilts rather than one vertical extrusion, aiming for fifteen to twenty outward facets across the whole rock, with every wall facet within forty-five degrees of vertical.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'the lip and floor split into several slightly differently angled planes with visible straight creases'. Primed measurement: 34 distinct uniform-tone facet regions on the rock, tones 87 to 162 either side of the field's 151, projected facet widths 1.4 to 11.7 mm, median facet area 55.2 mm2 and maximum 482.8 mm2, against round one's single unbroken tone over a constant 2.6-2.8 mm band.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The cavity wall between the rim and the pocket floor is large flat triangular planes at varying angles meeting the floor in straight lines, deep enough that the faceted inner wall is clearly visible as a band running all the way around.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'creases do run into and stop at pocket rims: one dies on the upper-left rim of the top-centre pocket and another terminates at the top-right pocket's rim', and the bottom-row pocket rims 'run off the flat floor and onto the sloped wall'. Primed: sampling a circle 0.4 mm outside each bore, cavity facets occupy 9% to 42% of the circumference at seven of the eight outer seats and 0% at the centre seat, which is correct because nothing is near it.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The nine seats stay perfectly circular, smooth-walled and flat-bottomed, bored straight down through whatever facets they meet, leaving the facet edges visibly interrupted at the pocket rims.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: the base reads as a thick slab meant to be set down, with an unbroken straight bottom edge in the isometric view and no foot, riser or relief beneath it. check_overhang at 45 degrees on all ten parts reports zero regions needing support and zero bridges.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The bottom face stays one flat plane so the board sits on a table and prints without supports.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'irregular blocky rubble with sharp wedge shards', 'a chaotic asymmetric rubble knot' with 'protruding shards', described as hard-edged and made only of flat polygons with no dome, sphere or lobe anywhere. The written solid carries 37 faces, which is five cubes plus a three-face foot with the fully buried faces consumed.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The bubble marker is a cluster of five interpenetrating cubes of clearly different edge lengths, largest 16.00 mm and smallest 7.00 mm, each rotated to its own distinct orientation about more than one axis so that square faces and corners jut out in many directions and no two cubes read as a repeated element.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: each cluster is one lumpy mass on its own round disc foot, low and wide, with nothing detached. Primed measurement: the marker envelope is 207 x 217 px, identical to the tooth's, and the cluster's plan silhouette is exactly its 206-208 px foot circle, so nothing leaves the footprint; the solid measures 26.000 mm tall with its greatest radius 13.78 mm against the 14.00 mm foot radius.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The cubes interpenetrate into one compact mound that is wider than it is tall, fused with the 28.00 mm foot into a single solid, exactly 26.00 mm tall and inside the 28.00 mm footprint.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'all four rubble pieces are identical copies of one sculpt, repeated and re-oriented'. Primed: sixteen of the thirty-six cell pairs are near-identical, exactly the ten tooth pairs plus the six bubble pairs, and no tooth matches a bubble.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: All four bubbles use this one geometry, exactly as all four of the retired lobed bubbles used one geometry.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: every hexagonal piece is one clean regular prism with a six-facet pyramidal cap on a round disc foot, all five identical. Primed: the held tooth in the signature sheet is pixel-for-pixel where it was in the previous round. measure/step-lineage.json shows all five tooth STEP exports reproduce the source archive's bytes exactly, and only the rind, the four bubbles and the assembly changed.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The tooth is not redesigned and is unchanged from the published set.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind, from the single-grey overhead image with no colour at all: 'Row 1: HEX, CLUST, HEX. Row 2: HEX, CLUST, CLUST. Row 3: CLUST, HEX, HEX. Plainly: unambiguous. The two silhouettes share no features - a crisp six-sided outline with a single central apex versus a lumpy asymmetric mass with protruding shards.' That grid matches the declared draw XOXXOOOXX exactly.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The two markers are tellable apart on silhouette alone, with no colour, from a seated player's view and from directly overhead.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: nine round sockets in a 3x3 grid, five hexagonal crystals and four rubble clusters and nothing else, and the signature sheet reads as 'a before and after of seating one crystal into the vacant top-right socket. Nothing else changes between panels.' Primed pixel checks: pitch 36.00 mm, foot 28.00 mm, board 140.20 x 130.17 mm, seat ring about 30 mm with the 1 mm annular clearance visible.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Tic-tac-toe is played unchanged: nine cells, two players, alternate placement into any empty cell, and ten printed parts - one rind, five teeth, four bubbles - with every fixed dimension preserved.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'Nothing reads translucent - all opaque flat fill.' Every surface in all four images is a solid flat tone with nothing showing through from behind, and the colourless overhead image renders the whole set in one opaque grey.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Every part is fully opaque: no translucency and no transparency anywhere, in the geometry or in the delivered colours.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: 'no fur, grit or micro-texture' anywhere, but it flagged 'knife-thin blade slivers' on the clusters. Measured, those are ordinary polyhedron edges, not features: the sharpest convex edge on the whole marker is a 42.0 degree wedge 0.79 mm long, every other convex edge is 47.8 degrees or blunter, the smallest face is 5.77 mm2, and check_thickness classifies all sub-minimum regions as tapers at feature edges, none as a wall - 0.07% of surface against a 2% budget, on a 14.60 mm median wall.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: No feature anywhere is thinner than 3.00 mm, and there are no needles, spikes, blades, fins, fur, grit, scattered micro-bumps or surface texture of any kind.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind flagged one floating piece, which is the staged held marker of the before-and-after sheet at the Wish's own 55.00 mm held offset and is seated in the after panel; it is presentation of the placement action, not a part of the product. check_overhang at 45 degrees on all ten parts reports zero regions needing support, zero bridges and a longest unsupported span of 0.0 mm.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: No face overhangs more than forty-five degrees from vertical, and nothing is unsupported or floating.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Blind: the rock carries no lines at all beyond facet creases and the nine seat rings, no raised lump stands out of any surface, and exactly three kinds of thing appear - one tray and the two marker families, ten pieces in total, with nothing added.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: No vein, crack network or raised second-material line on the rock; no druse, crust, bumps or surface texture; and no new component, insert, lid, storage tray or dice.

largest_risk: Physical printing, tactile handling, fit and durability remain untested, and the operator disabled motion verification for this run, so seating and withdrawal are unverified rather than passed. The nearest geometric risk is that the flat rim annulus is now the binding section at 3.154 mm against the 3.00 mm minimum wall, a margin under half a nozzle width; every millimetre of cavity band came out of that annulus, so any future request for a deeper or wider band cannot be met by widening outward without breaking the minimum wall, and would have to move crest heights or the field boundary instead.
resolution: Pass after one focused repair and a fresh review cycle. Round one was an unprimed blind read followed by the Wish reveal; it passed both markers and the whole manufacturing envelope but blocked the rind, measuring the cavity wall as a constant-width single-tone offset groove and the rock's top as one unbroken plane, so no facet edge was interrupted at any pocket rim. The repair put the facets where no dimension is pinned: the cavity crest vertices now sit at their own heights between 11.40 and 14.00 mm, the flat rim annulus is cut back to its 3.78 mm design width, and the field boundary is pulled to 13.00 mm from every outer seat axis so the bores cut the cavity facet base lines. Round two re-measured and cleared R4 and R5 and confirmed nothing regressed. Round three is an unprimed blind read of the exact sealed images, which independently reports the top as distinct facets with creases running into and stopping at pocket rims. The remaining flat field is forced by the Wish's own numbers - seats 2.00 mm deep with floors at 6.00 pin the field to 8.00 at every bore rim, and the 6.00 mm channel between neighbouring seats cannot carry relief without a sub-3.00 mm feature - and is disclosed rather than hidden.
reviewer: Independent native critics: one unprimed blind read of the sealed images, one primed requirement comparison over two rounds. The Manager did not self-review.
